```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Every number of the expected-numbers section is read from the committed data
# files of the case, so that the guide and the pages cannot drift apart; readr
# rather than datawizard::data_read(), which reads empty cells as "" rather than NA.
fmt <- \(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) |> sub(pattern = "^-", replacement = "−")

curve <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/spec_curve.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
analysts <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/analysts5.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
marks <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/reference_marks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
deviations <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/menu_deviations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
outcomes <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_outcomes.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
power <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_power.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ri <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_ri.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
n_emails <- nrow(readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/housing_audit.csv", show_col_types = FALSE))

ref <- datawizard::data_filter(curve, is_reference)
ref_all <- datawizard::data_match(curve, tibble::tibble(comparison = "white", population = "all",
                                                        uncoded = "drop", model = "lpm", adjust = "none"))
an <- \(id, col) analysts[[col]][analysts$id == id]
mark <- \(id) marks$b_pp[marks$id == id]
shift <- \(axis, option, col = "shift_mean") deviations[[col]][deviations$axis == axis & deviations$option == option]
pw <- \(design, gap) power$power[startsWith(power$design, design) & power$gap_pp == gap]
reply_gap <- datawizard::data_filter(outcomes, outcome == "reply" & contrast == "hispanic")
# The SCORE replication on the scale of the course (display_replication.csv)
replication <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
rep_val <- \(population_code, authorities_code, col) {
  replication[[col]][replication$population == population_code &
                       replication$authorities == authorities_code]
}
sgn <- \(x, d = 1) paste0(if (round(x, d) >= 0) "+" else "", fmt(x, d))

# The Task 3 test of 8PTRZ: Hispanic against all other names among the coded replies
coded <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(ProperName)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup))
tab_8ptrz <- stats::xtabs(~ hispanic_name + ProperName, data = coded)  # r-style: keep – the table that chisq.test() takes
chi_yates <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz)$statistic)
chi_plain <- unname(stats::chisq.test(tab_8ptrz, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# The Task 3 test of 25N5D: Hispanic against white names among the delivered
# emails, a missing reply counted as no greeting, with and without the
# continuity correction that prop.test() applies by default
counts_25n5d <- readr::read_csv("../cases/housing/data/audit_original.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  datawizard::data_filter(!is.na(Response_Dichotomous) & !grepl("^black", TreatmentGroup)) |>
  datawizard::data_modify(hispanic_name = grepl("^Hispanic", TreatmentGroup),
                          greeted = Response_Dichotomous == 1 & ProperName %in% 1) |>
  datawizard::data_summary(greetings = sum(greeted), emails = n(), by = "hispanic_name")
prop_yates <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails)$statistic)
prop_plain <- unname(stats::prop.test(counts_25n5d$greetings, counts_25n5d$emails, correct = FALSE)$statistic)

# Placement as try_spec() prints it: the specifications further below zero,
# with the tolerance of the helpers, so that the logit twin of the reference
# specification ties with it
placement_ref <- sum(curve$b_pp < ref$b_pp - 1e-9)
other_max <- deviations |>
  datawizard::data_filter(axis != "population") |>
  datawizard::data_summary(m = max(shift_max)) |>
  datawizard::data_extract("m")
```

::: {.callout-note}
**This document is for the facilitator.** It is rendered with the site but left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. It holds the run sheets of the four formats of the housing-audit case – the short session (deck `slides/housing-short.qmd`) and the one-day courses on open science, data tools and methods (decks `slides/housing-one-day-open-science.qmd`, `slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.qmd` and `slides/housing-one-day-methods.qmd`) – with the checks before a delivery, the expected numbers and the fallbacks. The participant pages under `tracks/` carry the same timings without the instructor guidance.
:::

## The formats {#formats}

| Format | Track | Taught in | What it leaves out |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short session, two halves of about 75 minutes | `housing-short` | the browser lab only | installation, the class chart, Task 5 |
| One day, open science | `housing-one-day-open-science` | the browser lab, the workspace as an option | the menu, the class chart, the run of Task 5 |
| One day, data tools | `housing-one-day-data-tools` | the browser lab, the workspace as an option (and recommended) | the menu, the class chart, Task 5 |
| One day, methods | `housing-one-day-methods` | the browser lab, the workspace as an option | nothing of the five tasks |

In every format the participant chooses which of the five reanalyses to reproduce in Task 3. Only the methods day sends results to the class chart. The segments that differ by format read the `deck:` map in the YAML of each deck through Quarto conditional content (`when-meta="deck.short"` and the like), so a change of wording for one format is made in the segment, inside the span or the div that carries that condition.

---

## The delivery lifecycle {#delivery-lifecycle}

Between deliveries the opening page advertises no delivery. Scheduling one takes three steps, and resetting after one takes two.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue, event, mode, registration URL), set `track:` to one of the four track slugs of the table above, and set `active: 'true'`. Render the opening page (`quarto render index.qmd`), and it shows a "Next delivery" callout with a link to the track. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide on recording. If you record, record the talk only, announce it at the start of each recorded stretch, and pause it for the hands-on tasks. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Decide which way the day leans. The decks keep optional runs on the `d` key: `tools` (five slides in the tools segment of Part 1 and the nine-slide R tutorial of Part 2) in the three one-day decks, and `methods` (the six-slide methods tutorial of Part 3 and the two slides of multiverse background in Part 4) in the methods deck, whose multiverse background is also the one optional run of the short session. The data-tools deck lists `tools` under `core-runs:`, so its tour of the toolchain and its R tutorial are part of the main flow. To make a run part of the main flow of another deck, list it under `core-runs:` in the YAML of that deck and render it again; a run that is not listed stays optional and can still be switched on live.

**Resetting, before the next delivery of the methods day.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and keep it as a dated snapshot, for example `cases/housing/data/class_results_2026-11-06.csv`.
- [ ] Clear the data rows of the Sheet, so that the chart opens almost empty for the next class. Do not touch the Form, the Worker or the field schema; only the rows change from one class to the next.

---

## Before the day

### The week before

- [ ] **The browser lab.** Every format is taught mainly in the browser lab, so check it on the published site in a real browser: the engine loads, the setup cell of Task 1 runs, and each of the five cells of Task 3 prints its value (the expected numbers are at the end of this guide).
- [ ] **The workspace repository.** The pages of the case are part of the course site, but the workspace (`CodeMoreh/replication-lab-housing`) does not exist on GitHub yet, and every address that points at it is a placeholder until it does: the workspace zip on the setup page and the cheatsheet, the workspace address on the tools slide of Part 1, and the links in the README of the workspace. Create the repository, push it, and download the zip once from its public address to confirm that it unzips into `replication-lab-housing-main`. The short session does not need it.
- [ ] **The class-results Form**, for the methods day only. Out of the box, the housing helpers submit to the results Form that every case shares, the one set up for the EU-frames case, and the housing chart reads the same Sheet through the same Worker, keeping only the rows whose label carries the word `housing` after the tag. That works as it stands. Clear the Sheet of the rows of earlier deliveries before the day (the data rows below the header of the tab "Form Responses 1"; the Form keeps working), because the EU-frames chart reads every row and would draw housing rows as unclassed diamonds. The alternative, which keeps the two classes apart for good, is a Form of its own, about twenty minutes once, following `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`.
- [ ] **Joining instructions.** Send the address of the track page, the case study as the pre-reading, and the request to open the browser lab once on the machine that each participant will bring, with a laptop charger. For the one-day courses add the setup page as optional, and as recommended for the data-tools day, with the request to run `R/check_setup.R` until it prints OK; add the help page.
- [ ] **The tab switching.** Click once through the sequences that you run live: the deck and the browser lab in every format; the deck, the specification menu and the decision map, and the Multiverse page in the short session and the methods day.
- [ ] **The room.** Confirm the projector, the power sockets, the wifi for visitors (webR downloads its engine and packages on first load) and whether the room has Vevox or a similar response tool. The slides say "type in chat" for the held answers; in the room, decide in advance what "chat" means, as the cue sheet below sets out.

### The night before

- [ ] Render the pages that have changed, page by page (pCloud breaks a full render), and check that the opening page, the track pages, the case pages and the deck of the day are current; push if the site is published.
- [ ] **The browser lab, cold.** Open the live page of the lab in a private window on a connection like that of the venue, time the load of the R engine, and run the setup cell and one cell of Task 3.
- [ ] **The live-results loop**, for the methods day. Submit one test result from the browser lab (`try_spec()`, then `submit_exploration(nickname = "test-row")`), confirm that it reaches the Sheet, press *Run Code* on the class chart of the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) page and find the test circle. Then delete the test row from the Sheet.
- [ ] **The workspace, as a participant meets it**, for the one-day courses. Download the zip afresh, unzip it, open the folder in your IDE, run `source("R/check_setup.R")` (every line OK, the last at −19.97 points) and render the report. For the data-tools day, also try the inline sentence of Part 4 and a clean run.
- [ ] **The public record**, for the open-science and methods days. Confirm that the three addresses of the records slide load without an account: doi.org/10.7910/DVN/1HOVTU, osf.io/3a8bg and osf.io/2ug8x, and that the final report of the replication is findable from the last one, because it is the target of the three-minute search in Part 4. The de-identified data of the replication are in its sub-component osf.io/xseqg, for anyone who asks.
- [ ] **The fallback zip**, for the one-day courses. Put the workspace zip on a USB stick, for anyone whose download fails in the room.
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card of the format (in its run sheet) as a ready-to-paste text, and charge everything.

### Opening the room

- [ ] Put the address of the course site, the browser lab and the cheatsheet on the screen or the whiteboard as people arrive, with the wifi details.
- [ ] Hand out the green and red sticky notes, or open the response tool, and say what each means: green, working; red, stuck.
- [ ] Keep the tabs of the day ready: the deck and the browser lab in every format, and in the short session and the methods day the [decision map](../cases/housing/map.qmd), the [specification menu](../cases/housing/menu.qmd) and the [Multiverse](../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) page.
- [ ] If you record, announce it now and say what is and is not recorded.

## Deck controls {#deck-controls}

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| space, right arrow or clicker | next slide, always exactly one: the deck is linear, so that no clicker press can skip a part |
| **`d`** | switch between the **extended** and the **lean** deck, live; in lean mode the optional slides are taken out of the deck and every key skips them |
| **`]`** and **`[`** | jump to the next or the previous part |
| **`g`** | jump bar: type a few letters of any slide title and press Enter |
| **`s`** | speaker view, with the notes, a timer and the next slide |
| **`f`**, **`esc`** | full screen, and the slide overview |

The readout at the top right names the part and the position, and its badge shows the state of the deck: green **extended**, burgundy **optional** on a slide of an optional run, amber **lean** when the runs are off, with a burgundy dot where a run has been lifted out. Adding `?depth=0` to the address opens the deck lean. The first slide of each optional run carries a small grey link that jumps to where the main flow resumes.

## Run sheet – the short session {#run-short}

The short session runs on `slides/housing-short.qmd` as two halves of about seventy-five minutes with a break of fifteen, entirely in the browser lab. It has no Task 2 at the keyboard (the estimand statement is written as a held answer, and the graph is followed on the slides), sends nothing to the class chart and has no Task 5; `tracks/housing-short/after.qmd` points to them for afterwards. Its one optional run is the two slides of multiverse background.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust**, here for an afternoon slot from 14:00 GMT.
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Example clock (GMT) |
|---|---|---|

| Break | 1:15–1:30 | 15:15–15:30 |
| Second half – Exploration and replication | 1:30–2:45 | 15:30–16:45 |

### Cutting order and what is never cut {#cutting-short}

For a slot of two hours, cut in this order: the multiverse background; the SCORE slide of the first half at speed; the slide on the linear probability model and the logit, to one sentence; the placement; and the replication to three slides (the design, the result, and robustness against replicability). The reproduction and the exploration keep their full time.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table; the held estimand statement; the box around the reply; the reproduction and its held answer; one try of `try_spec()` that changes the emails counted; robustness against replicability.

## Run sheet – one day, open science {#run-open-science}

The day runs on `slides/housing-one-day-open-science.qmd`, mainly in the browser lab. It has no menu of specifications, no class chart and no submission; Task 5 is filled in and not run. Its optional run is `tools`: five slides of the toolchain in Part 1 and the R tutorial of Part 2.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust.** The default starts at 10:00 GMT and keeps the breaks of the slides (thirty minutes, an hour, thirty minutes), so the day ends at 18:00. A 09:30 start ends at 17:30.
:::

| Segment | Elapsed | Clock (GMT) |
|---|---|---|
| Part 1 – Credibility and open research | 0:00–1:30 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Break | 1:30–2:00 | 11:30–12:00 |
| Part 2 – The claim and its estimand | 2:00–3:30 | 12:00–13:30 |
| Lunch | 3:30–4:30 | 13:30–14:30 |
| Part 3 – Reproduction | 4:30–6:00 | 14:30–16:00 |
| Break | 6:00–6:30 | 16:00–16:30 |
| Part 4 – Replication and preregistration | 6:30–8:00 | 16:30–18:00 |

| 0:08 | Talk: what social science is for, the crisis, the red-card study (20′) | Claims and checking; false positives and forking paths; the evidence; incentives and questionable research practices; the twenty-nine teams; the 'replication' crises. | Listen. | The red-card study returns in Part 2, so tell it in full only here. |
| 0:28 | Talk: the three Rs and open research (12′) | The data × analysis matrix; repeatability and credibility; the quick check, answered aloud; the practices of open research. | Answer the quick check. | The matrix is the slide to copy down. |
| 0:40 | Talk: SCORE and its three studies (20′) | The programme; the three studies, each with its result; the three Rs across SCORE. | Listen. | If behind, cut the data-availability slide of Miske et al. to one line. |
| 1:00 | Talk: Multi100 from the inside (8′) | What an analyst received, the two tasks, results on a common scale. | Listen. | – |
| 1:08 | Talk: the infrastructure (14′) | Open source; the toolchain; plain text and rendering; where data and code are archived; the lab and the workspace; what the tools cannot do. | Note the archives. | The archive slide is the one to cover in full; the tools run stays optional. |
| 1:22 | Task 1, the warm-up and the break (8′) | "Get the lab running; the warm-up asks which R each scenario is." | Setup cell; the warm-up. | Anyone stuck at the end of the break follows the shared screen. |

**The catch-up card**, for the re-entry to Part 3:

> Just back? You have missed nothing that you cannot recover: (1) if Task 2 is unfinished, keep the estimand statement that you wrote in chat; (2) Task 3 is the reproduction – choose one analyst in the browser lab, complete the cell, and compare your value with the table above the cells; (3) if you finish, reproduce a second analyst. Put up a red note and I will come to you.

If time is short, show it on the shared screen. |
| 0:46 | Hands-on 5: the preregistration block (30′) | "Fill in the block, copy it into your notes, swap with a neighbour." | Fill, copy, swap. | Say twice that nothing is run and nothing is sent. |
| 1:16 | Debrief on the swapped blocks (6′) | "Could your neighbour run your analysis from your block alone?" | Answer. | – |

### Cutting order and what is never cut {#cutting-open-science}

- **Part 1** – at 0:40, cut the data-availability slide of Miske et al. to one line and the open-research table to one sentence a row. At 1:08, leave the optional tools run switched off.
- **Part 2** – at 0:22, take the Lundberg slide in one sentence. At 0:52, skip the R tutorial. At 1:20, the graph is left out of Task 2.
- **Part 3** – at 0:45, the slide on the published model goes to one sentence. At 0:57, Hands-on 3b becomes a demonstration on the shared screen.
- **Part 4** – at 0:00, the curve goes to one sentence. At 0:32, show the three-minute search on the shared screen instead of setting it.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table; the held estimand statement; the reproduction and its held answer; what a reproduction needs; the preregistration of the replication against its report; robustness against replicability; a preregistration block filled in by every participant.

## Run sheet – one day, data tools {#run-data-tools}

The day runs on `slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.qmd`, mainly in the browser lab, with the workspace recommended because the IDE and the report have parts of their own. Its `tools` run is part of the main flow (`core-runs: [tools]`). It has no menu of specifications, no class chart and no Task 5. The curve appears once, near the end, as what the code makes possible.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft clock times for CM to adjust**, on the same clock as the other one-day courses: 10:00–18:00 GMT, with breaks of thirty minutes, an hour and thirty minutes.
:::

## Run sheet – one day, methods {#run-methods}

The day runs on `slides/housing-one-day-methods.qmd`, mainly in the browser lab, with the workspace as an option. It is the format with the robustness exercise at its centre: the menu, the class chart with its two waves of submissions, the curve of the claim and the declared analysis.

### Cutting order and what is never cut {#cutting-methods}

When time runs short, cut from the optional runs before anything else, so that the time comes out of a tutorial before it comes out of a task.

- **Part 1** – at 0:30, cut the data-availability slide of Miske et al. to one line and the open-research table to one sentence a row. At 0:58, leave the optional tools run switched off.
- **Part 2** – at 0:34, drop selection and feedback to one sentence. At 1:02, skip the R tutorial. At 1:22, Task 2 becomes a demonstration, finished over lunch.
- **Part 3** – at 0:50, the methods run stays off. At 1:05, Task 4 shortens to two calls of `try_spec()` and a submission, but everybody still submits.
- **Part 4** – at 0:10, skip the multiverse background. At 0:50, show the three-minute search on the shared screen instead of setting it.

**Never cut:** the five analysts and their table; the held estimand statement; the box around the reply; the reproduction and its held answer; the Task 4 submission; robustness against replicability; the preregistration moment.

## The held answers {#held-answers}

The class writes an answer, holds it and releases it together: the estimand statement (every format), the reproduced value of Task 3 (every format), the placement (the short session and the methods day) and "declared" before the preregistered run (the methods day only). Holding the answers keeps each one independent of the others, and releasing them together is what produces the matching values after the reproduction. The slides say "type in chat"; the cue sheet below says what that means in the room.

**The reproduction moment.** Each participant chooses one of the five analysts and runs that cell of Task 3, in the lab or in the workspace. When most of the class has a value: "Type the analyst and the value, hold it … go." Everyone who chose the same analyst should show the same value, and each value should match its record: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("8PTRZ", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for 8PTRZ, z = `r fmt(an("UYV3F", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for UYV3F, z = `r fmt(an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for EWFMI and $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("25N5D", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for 25N5D, with `r fmt(an("P9W8Y", "statistic_refit"), 3)` on 2 degrees of freedom for P9W8Y, which has nothing on record. A participant with `r fmt(chi_plain, 2)` for 8PTRZ or `r fmt(prop_plain, 2)` for 25N5D has passed `correct = FALSE`, which is the opening line of the next slide. A z of `r fmt(-an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` for EWFMI means that the Hispanic names are not the base group. A participant with another number has usually kept a different set of rows; check the filter against the table above the cells.

## In person and online {#cue-sheet}

The materials are the same in both settings. What changes is how people answer, flag trouble and pair up.

| Beat | In person (Newcastle) | Online |
|---|---|---|
| Held answers | the response tool of the room if it has one; otherwise written on a card and held up on "go" | typed in chat, sent on "go" |
| Working or stuck | green and red sticky notes on the laptop lid | a green circle or "STUCK" in chat |
| Rescues | the facilitator circulates | the problem shown on the shared screen |
| The live chart (methods day) | on the projector, and on the laptops | everyone opens the Multiverse page |
| Form links (methods day) | on the screen | pasted in chat |
| Breaks | the countdown slide and the time aloud | the countdown slide and "back at :xx" in chat |

## Fallbacks {#fallbacks}

Each row names the first move, not the only one, and every ladder ends at a point from which the session can carry on.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **The browser lab stalls** | The ladder of the [cheatsheet](../cases/housing/cheatsheet.qmd): a hard reload and the cells above run again, then a second browser, then the shared screen. On the methods day the last rung is the by-hand lookup, in which the facilitator reads the five choices off `spec_curve.csv` and submits the row through the Form, so that everyone still gets a mark. |
| **An installation fails on the day** | The browser lab holds the whole exercise and gives the same numbers; the participant carries on there, and the workspace survives for later. |
| **The workspace download fails in the room** | The zip on the USB stick. |
| **The wifi fails** | The workspace runs offline once its packages are installed, so the tasks continue for anyone who has it; the others follow the shared screen. On the methods day, collect the printed results (the tag, the label, `b`, `se`, `t`, `df`, `n`, `r`) and submit them through the Form when the network returns. The browser lab needs the network for its first load. |
| **The live chart fails** (methods day: Form, Worker, CORS) | The chart falls back to the committed `cases/housing/data/class_results.csv`, which holds only its header. Pull the Sheet as CSV, put it in place of that file, render the Multiverse page locally and share the screen. The static curve and the reference marks at the top of the page are enough for the debrief. Submissions are safe in the Sheet whatever happens to the chart. |
| **The OSF is slow during the three-minute search** | Show the report of the replication on the shared screen; the beat still works. Nothing in the tasks depends on the OSF. |
| **A participant has lost their tag** (methods day) | It is in `.class-tag` at the root of the workspace; in the lab, `report_result(nickname = "their-tag")` reuses it. |

## Expected numbers {#expected-numbers}

- **Task 1.** The setup cell of the lab: 1,014 rows and −19.97 percentage points. The last check of `R/check_setup.R`: the reference specification reproduces at `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` percentage points.
- **Task 2.** `r format(n_emails, big.mark = ",")` emails, 23 bounced, 991 delivered, 563 replies, 5 without a greeting code, 558 coded. Greeted by name among the coded replies: white 61.1%, Black 56.1%, Hispanic 41.2%; Santiago lowest at 37.1%. The graph: with every delivered email counted, the adjustment set is empty, because the name was assigned at random; the paths with `Z = "reply"` report the paths through the official and through the community as open. Adding the community to `Z` closes the second, and nothing can close the first, because nobody observed the official.
- **Task 3**, on the public file `audit_original.csv`. 8PTRZ: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(chi_yates, 3)` on `r an("8PTRZ", "n_recorded")` coded replies with the continuity correction, `r fmt(chi_plain, 3)` without it. UYV3F: z = `r fmt(an("UYV3F", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` on `r an("UYV3F", "n_recorded")` coded replies to Hispanic and white names. EWFMI: z = `r fmt(an("EWFMI", "statistic_recorded"), 3)` on `r an("EWFMI", "n_recorded")` coded replies, the row of the white names against the Hispanic base group. 25N5D: $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(prop_yates, 3)` on `r an("25N5D", "n_recorded")` delivered emails with the continuity correction of `prop.test()`, `r fmt(prop_plain, 3)` without it. P9W8Y: no recorded statistic; the likelihood-ratio test of the three groups gives $\chi^2$ = `r fmt(an("P9W8Y", "statistic_refit"), 3)` on 2 degrees of freedom for `r an("P9W8Y", "n_refit")` coded replies, the value in the text of the report of the analyst.
- **The reference specification** (white names, replies, uncoded dropped, linear model, no covariates): `r fmt(ref$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref$rate_comp)`%), t = `r fmt(ref$stat, 2)` on `r ref$df` df, n = `r ref$n`. Its twin on every delivered email: `r fmt(ref_all$b_pp, 2)` points (`r fmt(ref_all$rate_hisp)`% against `r fmt(ref_all$rate_comp)`%), n = `r ref_all$n`.
- **The curve.** `r nrow(curve)` specifications, all below zero and all significant at 5% under the test of the model, from `r fmt(min(curve$b_pp))` to `r fmt(max(curve$b_pp))` points; the largest p is `r fmt(max(curve$p), 4)`, and the largest randomisation p is `r fmt(max(curve$p_ri), 4)`. Counting every delivered email moves the estimate by `r fmt(shift("population", "all"), 2)` points on average (from `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_min"), 2)` to `r fmt(shift("population", "all", "shift_max"), 2)`); every other decision by at most `r fmt(other_max, 2)`. No pair changes its sign or its significance.
- **Placement.** The reference specification is placed at `r placement_ref`: no specification of the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it. A placement of 32 or more comes from counting every delivered email, because all 32 specifications that count the replies lie further below zero.
- **The reference marks.** OAs 2017 `r fmt(mark("OA"))` points (z = −3.73, N = 549); 8PTRZ `r fmt(mark("8PTRZ"))`; UYV3F `r fmt(mark("UYV3F"))`; EWFMI `r fmt(mark("EWFMI"))`; 25N5D `r fmt(mark("25N5D"))`; P9W8Y `r fmt(mark("P9W8Y"))`, placed by the course refit because Multi100 recorded no statistic for it. The published model refitted on the blinded thirds: `r fmt(mark("OA_blinded"))` points, not on the chart.
- **Replies.** The gap in any reply between Hispanic and white names is `r fmt(reply_gap$b_pp)` points, two-sided p = `r fmt(reply_gap$p, 2)`; the paper reports p = .11 with a one-tailed test.
- **Randomisation.** Reshuffling the names among the coded replies gives gaps between `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.025))` and `r fmt(quantile(ri$b_pp, 0.975))` points in 95% of `r format(nrow(ri), big.mark = ",")` reshuffles.
- **Power.** The original comparison, about 181 replies a group at a white share of 61%: `r fmt(pw("original", 20), 2)` for a gap of 20 points, `r fmt(pw("original", 13), 2)` for 13, `r fmt(pw("original", 10), 2)` for 10. The replication, 369 a group: `r fmt(pw("replication", 10), 2)` for 10 points.
- **The replication** (from its final report, osf.io/2ug8x): 3,050 authorities emailed, 1,811 replies; on the 1,243 replies of the authorities matched to census data, logit with the demographic covariates of the paper from the 2018 ACS (no Hard Email), b = 0.098 (SE 0.149), z = 0.66, p = 0.511 on a random draw of 738, and z = 0.44, p = 0.657 on all 1,243. The preregistered linear model was not significant "approximately 93 percent of the time". At most +2.45 points in favour of the Hispanic names. The plan was registered on 14 May 2020 (osf.io/v6wd8); the report lists the logit with covariates and the exclusion of the county authorities as deviations from it. The de-identified data are public at osf.io/xseqg (folder "Public Data": `Audit_Deidentified.dta`, the analysis do-file and a dictionary, licence unstated, so the course links to them and does not copy them). On the scale of the course (`cases/housing/data/display_replication.csv`), the gap is `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("replies", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies (`r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_hisp"))`% against `r fmt(rep_val("replies", "all", "rate_comp"))`%), `r sgn(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "b_pp"))` among the `r format(rep_val("replies", "sub-county", "n"), big.mark = ",")` replies of sub-county authorities, and `r sgn(rep_val("all", "all", "b_pp"))` points among all `r format(rep_val("all", "all", "n"), big.mark = ",")` emails in the de-identified file, none of them significant (smallest p = `r fmt(min(replication$p), 2)`). The logit with covariates in thirds on the 1,243 sub-county replies that carry every covariate (one of the 1,244 lacks the poverty third) gives b = 0.051, z = 0.45, column 4 of the report.
- **The five analysts.** Three concluded "evidence for the claim" in Task 1 of Multi100 (8PTRZ, UYV3F, EWFMI) and two "no evidence either way" (25N5D, judging the claim by the twenty points of the abstract; P9W8Y, whose Task 1 model tested the female names only).

---

## Debrief questions {#debrief}

Choose by what the class shows, not by the order below. Questions 1 to 3 and 8 need the class chart of the methods day; the others work in every format.

1. **The step in the curve.** "Who counted every delivered email? What question does your estimate answer that the estimate of the paper does not, and which one is the claim?"
2. **The decision that did nothing.** "Who changed the model from the linear probability model to the logit and found that the estimate barely moved? Why does it barely move here, when the coefficients look so different?"
3. **Placement.** "Your placement puts you among 64 justifiable alternatives. What does an analyst at the end of the curve owe the reader that an analyst in the middle does not?"
4. **The two verdicts of no evidence.** "Two analysts ticked 'no evidence', although the work of each shows a significant gap. What were they judging the claim by?"
5. **The reproduction.** "Everyone who chose the same analyst got the same value. What would have had to be missing for that to fail: the data, the code, or a default?"
6. **Robustness against replication.** "Every specification on these data finds the gap; the replication did not. Which result should a housing authority act on, and what would you want to know first?"
7. **The names.** "Santiago and Gabriela against Joe Garcia and Michael Hernandez. What does a name manipulate besides ethnicity?"
8. **How preregistration felt.** "Did writing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed? Would you have chosen differently after the exploration?"
